From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Markus / Kim — technical confirmation and proposed evidence list below. Apologies for the long note, wanted to be explicit for legal.

Edge caching behavior (summary):
- Purpose: short-lived inference KV and generated output prefix caching to reduce latency for repeated prompts.
- Residency: edge nodes may buffer tokens in memory and a transient LRU cache on local SSD for up to TTL (default 60s), but we do not persist user-level PII to long-term storage from edge nodes. Persistent logs are only written in designated regional clusters per the tenant's region mapping.
- Evidence we can provide: 1) reproducible run (small script + trace) showing TTL eviction at 60s; 2) sanitized dataflow capture PDF with node regions labeled (will mark any edge POPs and where failover occurs).

Onshore fallback design:
- If an edge POP cannot process requests, traffic routes to the nearest onshore regional cluster (US central / AWS us-east / us-west per customer's configured region) via our smart-router. Failover time: typically <2s for TCP rebind + routing, and <500ms additional processing depending on model.
- Proposed artifact: routing diagram + failing-node scenario trace (we can include a time series showing request routing switching to onshore).

Temp subprocessor / third-party CDN:
- We do integrate with select CDN partners for global acceleration; where customers require strict US-only processing we can block CDN caching at the edge and rely on regional clusters (this is a contract-level option).

Requested next steps:
- I will create: edge-ttl-eviction-trace.txt (sanitized), edge-dataflow-us.pdf, and a short failover-demo.mp4 (screen capture). ETA: 2026-11-06 EOD.

Grace O'Connor
Infrastructure Lead, Serving Runtime
